stem: A hospitalized client suddenly develops facial droop, arm weakness, and aphasia. The nurse activates the facility stroke alert. What is the main purpose of this activation?

options.A: Mobilize a coordinated stroke team for rapid assessment, brain imaging, and time-sensitive treatment decisions without waiting for a complete diagnostic workup before the response begins.
options.B: Replace bedside neurologic assessment because the stroke team will determine whether the deficits are real after imaging is complete.
options.C: Delay imaging until all laboratory and specialty consultations are completed so the diagnostic sequence is exhaustive before treatment decisions are made.
options.D: Use the alert only when stroke has already been definitively diagnosed, not when acute focal neurologic deficits are first recognized.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline emphasizes expeditious evaluation and treatment, organized stroke protocols, and immediate availability of a stroke team because reperfusion benefit is highly time dependent. Stroke-alert activation begins the coordinated response when stroke is suspected; it does not replace nursing assessment or require definitive diagnosis first. B, C, and D would create inappropriate delay or misunderstand the purpose of the emergency pathway.
educational_objective: Activate the stroke response promptly when acute focal neurologic deficits are recognized so a coordinated team can complete rapid assessment, imaging, and treatment decisions without avoidable delay.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_locator: Initial evaluation and stroke-systems sections: evaluation and initial treatment of suspected stroke should be performed expeditiously; organized protocols and availability of a stroke team speed clinical assessment, diagnostic studies, and early management decisions. Section 4.6.1 further emphasizes initiating eligible thrombolysis as quickly as possible and avoiding unnecessary diagnostic delays.
source_claim_supported: A stroke alert is an emergency systems-of-care activation used to mobilize rapid coordinated assessment, imaging, and treatment decisions for suspected acute stroke before a definitive diagnosis is fully established.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: recognize changes requiring rapid escalation, coordinate interdisciplinary care, and use emergency response systems appropriately.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — stroke-alert activation and rapid team coordination
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw generic stroke-code purpose item into a bedside deterioration scenario and corrected the blueprint from Safety & Infection Prevention and Control to Management of Care. The final item tests rapid systems activation without implying that the alert replaces neurologic assessment or requires a confirmed diagnosis first.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against the 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline's systems, team, imaging, and rapid-treatment principles.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reflects prompt coordinated evaluation. B wrongly replaces bedside assessment. C creates unsafe delay. D incorrectly requires definitive diagnosis before activation.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; rapid coordinated response to suspected stroke.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; unnecessary delay conflicts with time-sensitive stroke care.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; alerts are triggered by suspected acute stroke signs.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A captures both the timing and systems purpose of stroke-alert activation.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address how an acute stroke pathway should be activated and used.
audit_findings.blueprint: Emergency escalation and interdisciplinary coordination fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked whether 'stroke code' terminology is universal; because facilities use different names, the item uses the functional concept of a facility stroke alert rather than asserting one mandatory label. No second answer remained.
